correctness.rationale: The three construction branches exhaust all parameters; the crossing-prefix lower-quota bound follows from t<=a_1 and B<n, giving sum ceil(a_i/2)<=n<=sum a_i. Feasible integer quotas produce each selected part entirely as singleton/pair classes. Each class is independent; all unassigned goods are in unselected parts and conflict with every nonempty class, hence maximality. All class sizes differ by at most one, hence unit EF1. K3,3,3 impossibility of complete equitable 4-coloring follows from necessary 3,2,2,2 color sizes and indivisible three-item parts. Checker independently tested 7517 cases including 5118 with leftovers.

value.rationale: Theorem settles a natural infinite graph family for the maximal-equitable-partial-coloring existence problem explicitly posed in Equbal et al. Section 5.3, for every number of agents including n<=maximum degree where prior generic complete-coloring guarantees are inapplicable. K3,3,3 with four agents proves partial maximality is essential rather than a trivial complete-coloring corollary. The explicit linear-after-sorting construction isolates the role of exactly uniform item values against the known weighted bipartite obstruction.
